title: Volume 8 · Print Formats, Naming and Notifications
subtitle: Lessons 1–4: documents the customer can read, series numbers that survive an audit, and notifications that arrive once
outcomes: Build a print format from the builder without writing code
Set naming series per document type and branch so numbering stays gapless
Configure a notification that fires on the right event and only once
Standardise letterheads and terms so every document looks like one company

slides.title: Design a print format the customer will read
bullets: The print format builder gives you sections, fields and totals without a line of code
Print only the fields the customer needs: prices, quantities, tax and terms
Test with a real document, because a short address or a long item name breaks layouts
Attach a letterhead, or every invoice leaves the building looking improvised

rows: Document type Sales Invoice, standard format
Customer name, address, invoice number, date, due date
Seri Murni Sdn Bhd with registration and SST number

slides.notes: A print format is the only part of ERPNext most customers ever see, and it is judged in five seconds. Two rules cover most of it: put the tax number and the amount due at the bottom where people look, and never print internal fields such as cost or margin. Preview with the longest item name and the shortest address you can find.

slides.title: What a Malaysian invoice must show
bullets: Company name, registration and SST number are not optional on a tax invoice
Invoice number, date, customer details and item description must be legible
Tax must be shown as a separate amount, not folded into the rate
Terms and payment instructions reduce the number of calls to accounts
slides.notes: The three totals on the page must match the document to the cent, because an invoice that disagrees with the ledger is the fastest way to lose an accountant's confidence. Print one invoice and reconcile it line by line against the form before you hand the client a template. It takes five minutes and prevents months of quiet distrust.

slides.title: Series numbers that survive an audit
bullets: Naming series control document numbers, and gaps are the first thing an auditor asks about
Use the prefix fields rather than renaming series mid-year
Each branch or company needs its own series when documents are filed separately
Cancelled documents keep their number, because a reused number is worse than a gap

rows: 10 to continue after the last invoice

slides.notes: Gaps are acceptable when a document was cancelled; they are not acceptable when a series was renamed or restarted. Explain that distinction once, and the client's auditor will stop raising it as a finding. Align the prefix with the year and the company abbreviation, because the number is often the only identifier on a customer's remittance advice.

slides.title: Send the right message once, at the right moment
bullets: A notification watches one document event and applies a condition you write in plain fields
Send too many and people filter them, so target the exception rather than the routine
Use the document's own fields in the subject so the message is useful without opening it
Test with a real document and check the recipient list, not just your own inbox

rows: Document type Sales Order, event Submit
Role Sales Manager and the owner
Subject with order number, customer and total

slides.notes: Notifications are cheap to create and expensive to overuse, so the rule is one message per exception. A six thousand order triggering a note to the sales manager is a control; every order triggering a note is noise. Test with a document above and a document below the threshold, and check that the message arrives once rather than once per recipient plus the queue.

slides.title: One message, one recipient list, one test
bullets: A notification that fires twice trains people to ignore it, which defeats the control
Recipients should be roles or owners, not a typed list that rots after a resignation
The message must be useful without opening the document: number, customer, amount
Test above and below the condition, and check the queue for duplicates

rows: Sales Manager role plus document owner
order number, customer and total present
Click the link in the email

slides.notes: A notification is a control only if it is reliable, so test the failure case as carefully as the success case. Duplicate emails usually come from two notifications watching the same event, which is worth checking in the list before blaming the system. Keep one notification per exception and delete the rest.

slides.title: Make every document look like one company
bullets: A letterhead holds the logo, address and registration details used across all documents
Terms and conditions templates attach to quotations, orders and invoices without retyping
Both are configuration, so the client's team can maintain them after handover
Set a default so nobody has to remember to pick the right template

rows: Company name, address, registration, SST number
Terms and Conditions template Payment Terms
Header, terms and footer all present
Show the client how to edit both

slides.notes: These two settings are what make a system look finished, and they are also the easiest handover win. Show the client's administrator how to change an address or a term without a consultant, and they stop calling you for the small things. That is a commercial decision as much as a technical one.

slides.title: What a consultant configures without code
bullets: Everything in this volume is standard configuration, so it survives an upgrade
Print, series, notifications, letterhead and terms are all client-maintainable
Custom code is out of scope for a functional consultant, and usually unnecessary
Each item below has a named owner after handover
slides.notes: This page is the answer when a client asks for a custom print script: everything they actually want is here, in configuration, and it will still work after the next upgrade. Say that with confidence, because a functional consultant who reaches for code has left their own discipline.

slides.title: Testing print and notification changes
bullets: Test with a real document in a real state, never with a blank form
Check the edge cases: long names, many lines, zero tax, foreign currency
Keep a before and after copy of each template, so a change can be reversed
Re-test after every upgrade, because print and notifications are the first casualties
slides.notes: Testing is where most consultants lose an afternoon, so make it a checklist rather than an experiment. Five checks, five minutes, and the client sees a document they are happy to send. When an upgrade arrives, run the same five and you know within ten minutes whether anything broke.

lab.title: Lab · Brand the invoice, set the series and trigger one notification
steps: Create a letterhead with the company registration and SST number
Build a sales invoice print format with header, items and totals
Preview an invoice and confirm net 3,000.00, tax 240.00 and total 3,240.00
Set the naming series to SINV-SM-2026-.##### and continue from the last number
Create and cancel a document to confirm the number is not reused
Create a notification for sales orders above 5,000.00 on submit
Submit a 6,000.00 order and confirm exactly one email
Submit a 1,200.00 order and confirm no email
lab.done: Done when a printed invoice carries the registration and SST number with totals matching the ledger, the series is sequential without reuse, and the notification fires only above the threshold.

quiz.question: Where do you build a print format without code?
quiz.why: The Print Format Builder assembles sections, fields and totals through configuration, which survives upgrades and needs no development.

quiz.question: Why must cancelled documents keep their numbers?
options: Because reusing a number breaks the audit trail
quiz.why: A cancelled document is still a document, and reusing its number creates two documents with one identity, which auditors treat as a control failure.

quiz.question: A notification condition of grand_total greater than 5000 will fire for which order?
quiz.why: Only the 6,000.00 order exceeds the threshold. Testing both sides of the condition is part of configuring it.

quiz.question: Which detail should be absent from a customer-facing print format?
quiz.why: Cost and margin are internal. Printing them exposes commercial information to the customer and is a common builder mistake.

quiz.question: Who should own the letterhead after handover?
quiz.why: Letterheads and terms are configuration, so handing ownership to the client's administrator removes a recurring support cost and speeds small changes.

memory.spine: Documents customers can read, numbers an auditor can follow and messages that arrive once: three controls, all configuration, no code.

cards.q: What must a Malaysian tax invoice show?
cards.a: Company name, registration number and SST number, plus the tax breakdown per line.

cards.q: What do auditors ask about numbering first?
cards.a: Whether there are gaps or duplicates in the series, and who can edit the prefix.

cards.q: Why does a notification fire twice?
cards.a: It is attached to more than one event, or its condition matches both a draft and a submit.

cards.q: What should never be customised with code in this volume?
cards.a: Anything the print format builder or notification fields already do, because code does not survive an upgrade.

cards.q: How is a print format tested?
cards.a: With a real submitted document carrying real tax and a real address, never with a blank form.

trap.what: A notification is configured to fire on save as well as on submit.
trap.why: Every draft edit emails the customer, people stop reading the messages, and the control that catches late invoices is gone.

narration: Volume eight is where a functional consultant stops looking like an implementer. Print formats built in the builder give the customer a document worth reading, with the registration and tax number where they belong and totals matching the ledger to the cent. Naming series keep numbering sequential, and a cancelled document keeps its number because reusing one breaks the audit trail. Notifications watch a condition: an order above five thousand emails the sales manager, an order of twelve hundred stays quiet. Letterheads and terms templates make every document look like one company, and they are the easiest handover win because the client can maintain them alone. No code, all configuration, and it all survives the next upgrade. Test five things before handover: one page, matching totals, sequential numbering, one notification above the threshold and silence below it, and a letterhead the client can edit without calling you.
